newsitem.title: USA: Clinton approval rating highest since 1993 - poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton approval rating highest since 1993 - poll.

text.p: President Clinton's approval rating has reached its highest level since he took office in 1993, reaching the same level of 57 percent he attained shortly after he started his first term, a Newsweek magazine poll showed Saturday.
The 57-percent rating, which came on the eve of Clinton's second inaugural, was the same as the Newsweek poll showed in March 1993, two months after he took office.

The poll of 750 adults also showed disfavour with House Speaker Newt Gingrich who was re-elected to the leadership position despite ethics violations. The poll, taken Thursday and Friday, found that 57 percent thought the Georgia Republican should not continue as speaker.
The House ethics committee voted Friday night to recommend that Gingrich be reprimanded and required to pay a $300,000 penalty for his admitted breaches of House ethics rules.

The poll also found that despite his high rating, more people (46 percent) felt Clinton would rate in the bottom 10 among presidents than those who felt he would rate among the top 10 (37 percent) when ranked in 100 years.
